question: Differentiate $(\cos x)^x + x^{\cos x}$ with respect to $x$.
explanation:
Let $y=(\cos x)^x+x^{\cos x}$

For $(\cos x)^x$:
$\ln u=x\ln(\cos x)$
$\frac{du}{dx}=(\cos x)^x[\ln(\cos x)-x\tan x]$

For $x^{\cos x}$:
$\ln v=\cos x\ln x$
$\frac{dv}{dx}=x^{\cos x}\left[\frac{\cos x}{x}-\sin x\ln x\right]$

Thus,
$\frac{dy}{dx}=(\cos x)^x[\ln(\cos x)-x\tan x]+x^{\cos x}\left[\frac{\cos x}{x}-\sin x\ln x\right]$.

options.A: $(\cos x)^x[\ln(\cos x)+x\tan x]+x^{\cos x}\left[\frac{\cos x}{x}+\sin x\ln x\right]$
options.B: $(\cos x)^x[\ln(\cos x)-x\tan x]+x^{\cos x}\left[\frac{\cos x}{x}-\sin x\ln x\right]$
